findings.title: immediateDelete cancels in SendGrid but leaves the reminder row untouched
findings.body:
With `immediateDelete` the function cancels the batch and returns (lines 213-223). It neither deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row nor sets `cancelled`. The old code deleted the row. The SMS path and the `!referenceId` path still delete it. The row stays with `scheduled: true`, `cancelled: null` and the already-cancelled `referenceId` until the cron's `deleteMany` runs after `scheduledDate`.

The `handleNewBooking` reschedule path calls this with `true`. If the workflow step is edited before then, the step-edit branch in `workflows.tsx` (about line 567) picks up that stale row and calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(id, referenceId)`. That sets `cancelled = true`, so the cron sends a second cancel for a batch that is already cancelled. That request can fail, and one failure aborts the whole cron cancel loop (see the finding on `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`).

Delete the row after the cancel call succeeds. Cancelling then deleting would match the old behaviour, and the immediate path needs no flag.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancel pass, and no DB deletes run
findings.body:
The `try` wraps the whole `for` loop. The `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls are lazy Prisma promises that only execute when awaited in `Promise.all` after the loop (lines 66-74). If `client.request` throws for any reminder, the catch at line 75 runs. No delete has executed for the reminders already cancelled upstream, and no later reminder is processed.

There is no `orderBy`, so the same failing reminder can head the list on every 15-minute run. This keeps the later cancelled reminders from being cancelled until the failing row's `scheduledDate` passes and the first `deleteMany` removes it. Their emails then go to attendees of cancelled or rescheduled bookings, with only a `console.log` as a trace.

Try/catch per reminder, and `await` the delete right after each successful cancel. The query also doesn't filter `method: EMAIL`, which is harmless today because only email sets `cancelled`.

Separately, this file only calls `sgMail.setApiKey`. `client.setApiKey` lives in `emailReminderManager.ts`, which this route doesn't import. Please confirm `client.request` is authenticated in this route; the existing batch call at line 188 has the same dependency.

findings.title: Reminder DB cancellation is now fire-and-forget; the previous awaited delete is gone
findings.body:
Before, the reminder rows were removed through `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises that were awaited in `Promise.all`. Now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and not awaited. Only the SendGrid and Twilio calls were un-awaited before. The `update({cancelled: true})` and `delete` are now un-awaited too.

If the request finishes first, which can happen on serverless platforms, the flag or delete may never be written. The reminder then still goes out to the attendee of a cancelled booking, and nothing signals it.

The same applies to `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` lines 489-493, where the old `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed, and to the `workflows.tsx` call sites (about lines 212, 376, 519, 574). Collect the returned promises and await them with `Promise.all`. Also drop the `async` on the `remindersToUpdate.forEach` callback at `workflows.tsx` line 574, which is pointless.

findings.title: try/catch cannot catch errors from the un-awaited reminder cancellations
findings.body:
`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` return promises that are neither awaited nor collected. The `try/catch` at lines 964-975 therefore guards nothing, and `log.error` is unreachable for their failures. The functions already swallow their own errors with `console.log`. Either await them (`await Promise.all(...)`) so the catch means something, or remove the wrapper.

This reschedule path uses `immediateDelete = true` for email, while the trpc reschedule path in `bookings.tsx` line 490 uses the deferred flag. Please say why the two differ.

findings.title: Commented-out block was de-indented by the diff, and unused imports remain
findings.body: Lines 901-962 sit inside a `/* ... */` comment that was already there. This PR strips the indentation from its code lines (the diff shows these as changed lines with no logical change). That is unrelated churn and makes the block harder to read; revert it. Also, `Prisma` is added to the value import at line 9 (without a trailing comma), but the only uses of `Prisma.` were deleted in this PR, so it is now unused. `PrismaPromise` is still used at line 342, but it is a type and should stay in a type-only import as before.

findings.title: Type-only imports turned into value imports
findings.body: `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput` and `Prisma` (used only as a type namespace) were previously imported with `import type`. They are now in a value import together with the enums. Keeping `import type {...}` for the types avoids pulling them into the value import and keeps `isolatedModules` and lint rules happy.

findings.title: Unrelated UI change bundled into a reminder-cancellation PR
findings.body: The wrapper changes from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) &&` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded &&`, and the inner block is re-indented. This looks like it fixes an empty grey box shown when only a sender ID is needed (the sender block is rendered separately at line 463). That is a behaviour change unrelated to cancelling reminders. It would be better as its own PR, or at least mentioned in the description.

contracts.action: Email reminder cancellation now sets `cancelled = true` and defers the SendGrid cancel to the cron
contracts.equivalent_path: Old `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(referenceId)` posted a SendGrid cancel and then sent a DELETE immediately; the callers then deleted the row.
contracts.before_after: Before, the batch was cancelled in SendGrid at once and the row deleted by the caller. Now the default path only flags the row (lines 225-232). The cron (`scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-77`) cancels and deletes rows whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. It runs every 15 minutes, so cancellation lands between about 45 and 60 minutes before send.
contracts.visible_effect: The attendee or host is not emailed after cancel or reschedule, provided the cron succeeds before the send time.
contracts.failure_mode: A thrown SendGrid error aborts the whole cancel loop and the lazy deletes never run (finding on scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56). The flag write is not awaited by callers, so it can be lost on early termination.

contracts.action: Reschedule in handleNewBooking cancels the old booking's reminders
contracts.before_after: The other two paths use the deferred flag for email. This one uses `immediateDelete = true`, so the SendGrid cancel happens at once and the row is left in place.
contracts.visible_effect: The old reminder email is cancelled right away. The stale row stays until `scheduledDate` passes.
contracts.failure_mode: Errors are swallowed inside the callee, so the surrounding try/catch is dead. The stale row can later be re-flagged by a workflow edit and double-cancelled.

contracts.action: SMS reminder cancel now also deletes the DB row inside the manager
contracts.equivalent_path: Old callers ran `workflowReminder.deleteMany` awaited alongside the Twilio cancel.
contracts.before_after: Row deletion moved into the manager, un-awaited by callers. When Twilio `cancelSMS` throws, the delete is skipped and the row remains. In the workflow-delete path the cascade can delete the row first, so the later `delete` throws P2025, which is caught and logged.
contracts.visible_effect: The SMS is cancelled in Twilio and the row removed. If the callers' work is cut short, the row remains.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed Twilio cancel is logged only. The row stays with no cancelled flag and no retry.

summary: Reminder cancellation moves from an immediate SendGrid cancel to a `cancelled` flag that the cron processes. I found two problems. The `immediateDelete` branch leaves the DB row behind, which can lead to a double-cancel. The cron's cancel loop gives up entirely on the first SendGrid error, so later reminders are not cancelled and attendees of cancelled bookings can still get emails. The DB cancel and delete calls are also no longer awaited by callers, which was an awaited delete before. The rest is cleanup: a try/catch that guards nothing, a de-indented comment block with an unused import in `workflows.tsx`, and type imports turned into value imports. The migration and schema agree. I did not run or test anything.
